vo.text: That's Mrs. Lan. Power out two days since the ice storm. She doesn't read English. She just left a voice note for her neighborhood hotline. Watch the clock.
She heard it read back in Vietnamese and said yes. The group's own rules, not the AI, set the amount: a hundred and fifty dollars. Two organizers, on two phones.

text.sandbox: Paid, into her Venmo, with a message in Vietnamese. {T_words} seconds from voice note to PayPal's SUCCESS webhook. Our organizers tapped on cue; with real volunteers, it's as long as two neighbors take to check their phones.
text.fake: Paid, into her Venmo, with a message in Vietnamese. {T_words} seconds from voice note to the SUCCESS webhook, on our PayPal stand-in. Our organizers tapped on cue; with real volunteers, it's as long as two neighbors take to check their phones.

vo.text: This is Neighborline: a hotline, not a dashboard. After the Eaton fire, one LA mutual-aid network took three hundred requests overnight, in Instagram comments. Most groups still run on spreadsheets and a volunteer's personal Venmo.
Rosa asks for groceries, in Spanish. Same rules, two approvals.
Her email has no PayPal account yet, so PayPal reports the payout unclaimed.
Most systems stop there. Neighborline messages her, in Spanish, exactly how to claim it.
Someone posing as the organizers, with a Venmo handle one letter off? Approve is disabled on every phone. No money moves.

vo.note: Retimed: the script gives part 1 only 1:36–1:46 (37 words = 222 wpm). It now runs into Shot 10.
vo.text: Under the hood: the agents that talk to neighbors have no PayPal tools at all. One separate approval service holds the Payouts credentials, and it pays only on a record signed with the passkeys of two different organizers.

vo.note: Retimed: runs over code card 1, which is the schema-repair card it describes.
vo.text: Every AI output is checked against a schema, repaired once, or the neighbor is asked again, never guessed.
The batch ID is a hash of that approval, so a double tap can't pay twice. Webhooks are signature-verified, and every payout is reconciled against PayPal Transaction Search.

Donors give with PayPal or Venmo. The public report is AI-written around numbers that code pulls from the ledger, and it never names a neighbor. Built for the roughly nine hundred volunteer groups that mobilize when the storm hits.
Neighborline is open source. Try the hotline yourself, no login, at the link below. Because the morning after a storm, help should sound like your own language.
